HOUSE BILL NO. 5786
A bill to require that contracts for the construction of an
enterprise data center include certain provisions; to require certain hiring
practices for the construction of an enterprise data center; to provide for the
powers and duties of certain state governmental officers and entities; to
require the submission and maintenance of certain documents; to prescribe
sanctions; and to allow for the submission of complaints.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. This act may be
cited as the "
enterprise data center
construction labor
act".
Sec. 2. As used in this
act:
(a) "Construction" means the construction, erection,
reconstruction, alteration, conversion, demolition, repair, moving, or
equipping of buildings or structures.
(b) "Construction
contract" means a contract for the construction of an enterprise data
center as described in section 3.
(c)
"
Enterprise data
center" means
that term as defined in section 4ee of the general sales
tax act, 1933 PA 167, MCL 205.54ee.
(d)
"Labor
organization" means that term as defined in section 2 of 1939 PA 176, MCL
423.2.
(e) "Locality" means the
county or prosperity region in which an enterprise data center is located, as
determined by the Michigan strategic fund.
(f) "Michigan strategic
fund" means the Michigan strategic fund as created under section 5 of the
Michigan strategic fund act, 1984 PA 270, MCL 125.2005.
(g) "Registered apprenticeship
program" means that term as defined in 29 USC 50c or a program registered
with a state apprenticeship agency recognized by the United States Department
of Labor.
Sec. 3.
(1) The owner of an enterprise data center, or the owner's
designee,
shall not
enter into a
construction
contract for the construction of
an enterprise
data center unless the
construction
contract requires that the contractor
or subcontractor
make a good-faith effort in
accordance with this act to do both of
the following
:
(a) Use the following
order
of priority in
recruiting and
hiring workers
to construct the
enterprise
data center:
(
i
)
Workers
who are members of a labor organization in the locality in which the
enterprise
data center is being constructed.
(
ii
)
Workers
who are members of a labor organization in this state but outside the locality
in which the
enterprise
data center is being
constructed.
(
iii
)
Workers
who are members of an out-of-state labor organization.
(b) Except for a job classification
that the Michigan strategic fund determines registered apprentices are not
reasonably available to perform, ensure that not less than 10% of the total
labor hours performed on the construction of the enterprise data center is performed
by apprentices enrolled in a registered apprenticeship program.
(2) A contractor or subcontractor
subject to a construction contract shall do both of the following:
(a) Document the contractor's or
subcontractor's good-faith efforts required by the construction contract.
(b) Maintain the documents described
in subdivision (a) for not less than 3 years after construction of the
enterprise data center is complete, or a longer period if prescribed by the
Michigan strategic fund.
(3) The Michigan strategic fund
shall prescribe a manner in which a contractor or subcontractor must maintain a
document that evidences the contractor's or subcontractor's good-faith efforts
required by a construction contract.
(4) The Michigan strategic fund may
determine, in writing, that registered apprentices are not reasonably available
for 1 or more job classifications during a specified period.
Sec.
4. To demonstrate a good-faith effort to hire or recruit workers in the order
of priority described in section 3, a contractor or subcontractor shall, at a
minimum, do all of the following:
(a) Submit a written request for
referral of qualified workers to at least 1 labor organization in the locality
that customarily supplies workers for the relevant job classification that the
contractor or subcontractor is recruiting or hiring. The written request must
include the job classification, anticipated start date, expected duration, work
location, shift information, pay scale, and number of workers requested.
(b) After the contractor or
subcontractor submits a request under subdivision (a), wait not less than 3
days for the labor organization to respond to the request.
(c) If the labor organization
responds to the request that it cannot refer a sufficient number of qualified
workers, or if the labor organization does not respond within the 3-day time
period, proceed to the next priority level described in section 3. The
contractor or subcontractor must maintain the labor organization's response or
proof of delivery of the written request, as applicable.
(d) If the contractor or
subcontractor recruits or hires workers from outside the enterprise data
center's locality, maintain documentation that shows why workers were not
available from the higher-priority level for that job classification and work
period that the contractor or subcontractor is recruiting or hiring for.
(e) Document each action described
in this section.
Sec.
5. An owner of an enterprise data center, or the owner's designee, that enters
into a construction contract shall submit, in the form, manner, and frequency
prescribed by the Michigan strategic fund, a sworn certification and workforce
report that verifies, as determined by the Michigan strategic fund, that the
contractor or subcontractor subject to the construction contract is in
compliance with the contractual requirements described in section 3 and is demonstrating
a good-faith effort under section 4. The workforce report must identify the
workforce that the owner uses in the construction of the enterprise data center
and include all of the following:
(a) The job classification of each
worker.
(b) The total number of hours worked
on the construction of the enterprise data center and the total hours worked by
each worker.
(c) The recruiting sources that were
used to hire the workers.
Sec.
6. (1) If the Michigan strategic fund determines that a construction contract
violates section 3 or the contractor or subcontractor subject to a construction
contract fails to demonstrate a good-faith effort under section 4, the
enterprise data center is subject to 1 or both of the following:
(a) Being ineligible for the tax
exemptions provided under section 4ee of the general sales tax act, 1933 PA
167, MCL 205.54ee, and section 4cc of the use tax act, 1937 PA 94, MCL
205.94cc.
(b) As determined by the Michigan
strategic fund, suspension or revocation of a certificate issued by the
Michigan strategic fund under section 4ee of the general sales tax act, 1933 PA
167, MCL 205.54ee, or section 4cc of the use tax act, 1937 PA 94, MCL 205.94cc.
(2) If the Michigan strategic fund
determines that both of the following events occurred as related to an
enterprise data center, the Michigan strategic fund shall notify the department
of treasury:
(a) One or both of the following
violations:
(
i
)
The construction contract violates section 3.
(
ii
)
The contractor or subcontractor subject to the construction contract fails to
demonstrate a good-faith effort under section 4.
(b) A tax exemption under 1 or both
of the following was applied to the enterprise data center during the time that
1 or both of the violations described in subdivision (a) occurred:
(
i
) Section
4ee of the general sales tax act, 1933 PA 167, MCL 205.54ee.
(
ii
) Section
4cc of the use tax act, 1937 PA 94, MCL 205.94cc.
(3) The Michigan strategic fund may
do both of the following to implement the requirements of this section:
(a) Audit, inspect, or otherwise
review documents that a person is required to maintain under this act to
determine compliance with this act.
(b) Require a person to submit
supplemental workforce reports or documentation that the Michigan strategic
fund determines is necessary to determine compliance with this act.
Sec.
7. (1) A labor organization in the locality in which an enterprise data center
is being constructed, or an individual worker, may submit a complaint to the
Michigan strategic fund that the contract for the construction of an enterprise
data center violates this act. The complaint must be submitted in writing and
have supportive documentation.
(2) Upon receipt of a complaint
under subsection (1), the Michigan strategic fund may review the complaint and
request additional information from the applicable contractor, subcontractor,
or owner of the enterprise data center to determine if the construction
contract violates this act.
Sec.
8. This act must not be construed to do any of the following:
(a) Require a person to enter into a
project labor agreement.
(b) Prohibit the hiring of a worker
who is not a member of a labor organization if other workers are not reasonably
available under the order of priority described in section 3.
(c) Limit the Michigan strategic
fund's authority to prescribe forms and reasonable documentation standards to
administer this act.
Enacting section 1.
This act does not take effect unless both of the following bills of the 103rd
Legislature are enacted into law:
(a) House Bill No. 5787 (request no. H05629'25).
(b) House Bill No. 5785 (request no. H05769'25).

2026-HB-5952.title: House Bill 5952 of 2026
2026-HB-5952.subject: Worker's compensation: benefits; post-traumatic stress disorder injury fund; create. Amends1969 PA 317(MCL418.101-418.941) by adding sec. 409.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Mike Mueller

2026-HB-5952.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 5952
A bill to amend 1969 PA 317, entitled
"Worker's disability compensation act of
1969,"
(MCL 418.101 to 418.941) by adding section 409.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 409. (1) The
post-traumatic stress injury fund is created in the state treasury.
(2) The state treasurer shall deposit money and other assets received
from any source in the fund. The state treasurer shall direct the investment of
money in the fund and credit interest and earnings from the investments to the
fund.
(3) The director is the administrator of the fund for audits of the
fund.
(4) The director shall expend money from the fund on appropriation, only
for 1 or more of the following purposes:
(a) To pay claims authorized under section 407.
(b) To pay costs to administer the post-traumatic stress injury fund.
(5) If there is insufficient money in the fund to pay claims authorized
under section 407, claims that are approved but not paid must be paid if fund
revenues become available, and those claims must be paid before subsequently
approved claims. The director shall develop and implement a process to notify
the legislature that money in the
post-traumatic stress
injury
fund may be insufficient to cover future claims if at any time the
director reasonably believes that within 60 days the money in the fund will be
insufficient to pay claims. The process must, at a minimum, do all of the
following:
(a) Identify a specific date by which the money in the fund will become
insufficient to pay claims.
(b) Outline a clear process indicating the order in which claims pending
with the fund will be paid.
(c) Outline a clear process indicating the order in which claims that
were pending with the fund when money became insufficient will be paid, if
money subsequently becomes available.
(6) The director shall submit an annual report to the state budget
director and the senate and house of representatives standing committees on
appropriations not later than April 1 of each year that includes, but is not
limited to, all of the following:
(a) The total number of claims received under the post-traumatic stress
injury fund in the immediately preceding calendar year.
(b) The number of claims approved and the total dollar amount of claims
paid by the post-traumatic stress injury fund in the immediately preceding
calendar year.
(c) The costs of administering the post-traumatic stress injury fund in
the immediately preceding calendar year.
(7) By March 31 of each year, the agency shall report to the chairs of
the appropriations committees of the senate and the house of representatives
the estimated amount of both of the following:
(a) The anticipated cost of benefits in the next fiscal year for claims
authorized under section 407 and payable by the post-traumatic stress injury
fund.
(b) The amount of any anticipated shortfall in the post-traumatic stress
injury fund that would prevent payment of claims for the current fiscal year.
(8) The post-traumatic stress injury fund has the same rights under this
act as an employer or carrier.
Enacting section 1.
This amendatory act does not take effect unless Senate Bill No. ____ (request
no. S06709'26) or House Bill No. ____ (request no. H06709'26) of the 103rd
Legislature is enacted into law.

2026-HB-5953.title: House Bill 5953 of 2026
2026-HB-5953.subject: Worker's compensation: disabilities; presumption of causation of post-traumatic stress disorder; provide for certain occupations and allow for claims against post-traumatic stress injury fund. Amends1969 PA 317(MCL418.101-418.941) by adding sec. 407.   TIE BAR WITH:HB 5952'26

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Mike McFall

2026-HB-5953.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 5953
A bill to amend 1969 PA 317, entitled
"Worker's disability compensation act of
1969,"
(MCL 418.101 to 418.941) by adding section 407.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 407.
(1)
Subject to subsection (4), an eligible individual who makes a claim for
benefits against the eligible individual's employer for work-related
post-traumatic stress disorder shall suspend the claim and may make a claim for
like benefits from the post-traumatic stress injury fund if the eligible
individual meets both of the following conditions:
(a) Experiences a qualifying traumatic event on or after the effective
date of the amendatory act that added this section in the course of the eligible
individual's employment in an occupation described in subsection (9)(a)(
i
).
(b) Is diagnosed after the qualifying traumatic event with
post-traumatic stress disorder by a mental health professional.
(2) If an eligible individual makes a claim against the fund under
subsection (1), except as otherwise provided under subsection (3), the
post-traumatic stress disorder is presumed to arise out of and in the course of
employment.
(3) The presumption under subsection (2) may be rebutted by clear and
convincing medical evidence that 1 of the following applies:
(a) The eligible individual's post-traumatic stress disorder was
primarily caused by non-work-related factors.
(b) The diagnosis does not meet the diagnostic criteria of the most
current edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
(4) As a condition precedent to filing an application for like benefits
under subsection (1), an eligible individual must first apply for and do all
things necessary to qualify for any pension benefits to which the eligible
individual, or the eligible individual's decedent, may be entitled or must
demonstrate that the eligible individual or the eligible individual's decedent
is ineligible for any pension benefits. If a final determination is made that
pension benefits will not be awarded or that the eligible individual or the
eligible individual's decedent is ineligible for any pension benefits, then the
presumption under subsection (2) applies. The employer or eligible individual
may request 2 copies of the determination denying pension benefits, 1 copy of
which must be filed with the agency on request.
(5) If an eligible individual described in subsection (1) is eligible
for any pension benefits, that eligibility does not prohibit the eligible
individual or dependents of that eligible individual from receiving benefits
under section 315 for the medical expenses or portion of medical expenses that
are not provided for by the pension program.
(6) An eligible individual's suspension of a claim under subsection (1)
is in effect only during the period the eligible individual receives like
benefits from the fund. If a redemption agreement between the fund and the
eligible individual is approved, the suspension of a claim against the eligible
individual's employer under subsection (1) continues indefinitely.
(7) If an application for a hearing filed with the agency concerns
post-traumatic stress disorder, a hearing must be held not later than 90 days
after the application is received, and, except for a hearing that concerns a
case described under section 205, must take precedence over all other hearings.
(8) The director shall develop the application, approval, and compliance
process necessary to operate and manage the fund. The director shall develop
and implement the use of an application form to be used by a claimant for
benefits payable by the fund under subsection (1). When a claim under
subsection (1) is received, the director shall notify the employer against whom
a claim is suspended or the carrier. The employer or carrier may access all
information the agency receives with respect to the claim and may request that
the agency obtain specific additional information. The fund standards,
guidelines, and templates, and any other forms used by the director to
implement the fund must be posted and maintained on the department's website.
The director shall review and consider claims in the order in which they are
received and shall approve or deny a claim not later than 30 days after receipt
of the claim.
(9) As used in this section:
(a) "Eligible individual" means an individual who meets all of
the following requirements:
(
i
) Is or was at
the time the individual experienced a qualifying traumatic event 1 of the
following:
(A) A full-time, part-time, paid on-call, or volunteer member of a fire
or police department of a city, township, or incorporated village.
(B) A full-time, part-time, paid on-call, or volunteer member of a
public fire authority.
(C) A county sheriff or a full-time, part-time, paid on-call, or
volunteer deputy of the county sheriff.
(D) A full-time, part-time, paid on-call, or volunteer member of the
state police.
(E) A full-time, part-time, paid on-call, or volunteer member of a fire
department of an airport operated by a county, public airport authority, or
state university or college.
(F) An individual who holds a license under section 20950 of the public
health code, 1978 PA 368, MCL 333.20950.
(G) A state correctional officer as that term is defined in section 2 of
the correctional officers' training act of 1982, 1982 PA 415, MCL 791.502.
(H) A 911-dispatcher or call taker.
(
ii
) Has 5 or more
years of cumulative service in an occupation described in subparagraph (
i
).
(
iii
) If the
individual is retired from an occupation described in subparagraph (
i
), has been retired for fewer than 10
years.
(
iv
) Files a claim
not later than 180 days after learning of the post-traumatic disorder diagnosis
and its relationship to the individual's employment.
(b) "Fund" means the post-traumatic stress injury fund created
under section 409.
(c) "Mental health professional" includes all of the
following:
(
i
) A doctoral
level psychologist licensed under section 18223(1) of the public health code,
1978 PA 368, MCL 333.18223.
(
ii
) A psychologist who
is licensed or otherwise authorized to engage in the practice of psychology
under part 182 of the public health code, 1978 PA 368, MCL 333.18201 to
333.18237.
(
iii
) A licensed master's
social worker as that term is defined in section 18501 of the public health
code, 1978 PA 368, MCL 333.18501.
(
iv
) A licensed
professional counselor as that term is defined in section 18101 of the public
health code, 1978 PA 368, MCL 333.18101.
(
v
) Any other
practitioner licensed in this state with a master's degree or higher who is
qualified under state law to diagnose post-traumatic stress disorder.
(d) "Post-traumatic stress disorder" means a mental disorder
that meets diagnostic criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder under the
most recent edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental
Disorders.
(e) "Qualifying traumatic event" means a high-stress situation
that may lead to psychological trauma. Qualifying traumatic event includes, but
is not limited to, all of the following:
(
i
) Witnessing or
responding to another individual's serious bodily injury or death.
(
ii
) Receiving
immediate threats to life or safety.
(
iii
) Witnessing or
responding to a mass casualty incident.
(
iv
) Responding to
or investigating crime scenes.
(f) Qualifying traumatic event does not include any of the following:
(
i
) Disciplinary
actions.
(
ii
) Personnel or
performance evaluations.
(
iii
) Job transfers,
layoffs, demotions, or terminations.
Enacting section 1. This amendatory act does not take
effect unless Senate Bill No. ____ (request no. S06746'26) or House Bill No. 5952
(request no. H06746'26) of the 103rd Legislature is enacted into law.

2026-HB-5954.title: House Bill 5954 of 2026
2026-HB-5954.subject: Labor: hours and wages; scheduling standards for certain employers; provide for. Creates new act.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Kara Hope

2026-HB-5954.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 5954
A bill to require certain employers to provide written work
schedules to certain employees; to require compensation for changes to a work
schedule in certain circumstances; to allow employees to request changes to
work schedules; to prohibit employers from requiring employees to work during
certain rest periods; to require certain notices and postings; to prohibit
retaliation; to provide for the powers and duties of certain state governmental
officers and entities; to provide for the promulgation of rules; and to provide
remedies.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. This act may be
cited as the "employee fair scheduling act".
Sec. 3. As used in this
act:
(a) "Chain" means an establishment that is part of
an affiliation of 2 or more establishments in the United States owned by the
same person and
that
operate under an
identical or substantially similar trade name or mark as those terms are
defined in section 1 of 1969 PA 242, MCL 429.31.
(b) "Department" means the department of
labor and economic opportunity.
(c) "Employee" means, subject to subdivision (d), an
individual who is employed by an employer and
provides
services
in that employment
related to any of
the following at a retail establishment, hospitality establishment, or food
services establishment:
(
i
)
Retail trade, as that term is used in code 44-45 of the 2012 North American
Industry Classification System.
(
ii
)
Hotels or motels, as those terms are used in code 721110 of the 2012 North
American Industry Classification System.
(
iii
)
Food services, as that term is used in code 722 of the 2012 North American
Industry Classification System.
(d) "Employee" does not include any of the
following:
(
i
)
An individual engaged in administrative, executive, or professional work and to
whom all of the following apply:
(A) Performs predominately intellectual, managerial, or
creative tasks.
(B) Exercises discretion and independent judgment.
(C) Earns a salary and is paid on a salary basis.
(
ii
)
An individual employed by an employer to perform services for a client of the
employer if the employer's primary business is to provide clients with the
temporary services of 1 or more individuals who are under contract with the
employer.
(e) "Employer" means a person
,
including, but not limited to, a chain or integrated
enterprise, that employs
20
or more
individuals worldwide and is a retail establishment, hospitality establishment,
or a food services establishment. The number of individuals employed by an
employer
is
determined based on the average
number of individuals employed on each working day during each of 20 or more
workweeks in the current calendar year or immediately preceding calendar year.
(f) "Food services establishment" means the fixed
point of sale location for establishments defined as food services and drinking
places in code 722 of the 2012 North American Industry Classification System.
(g) "Hospitality establishment" means a hotel or
motel as those terms are used in code 721110 of the 2012 North American
Industry Classification System, or a casino hotel as that term is used in code
721120 of the 2012 North American Industry Classification System.
(h) "Integrated enterprise" means 2 or more separate
entities, 1 of which controls the operations of the others, as determined based
on the following factors:
(
i
)
The degree of interrelation between the operations of multiple entities.
(
ii
)
The degree to which the entities share common management.
(
iii
)
The degree to which the entities have centralized control of labor relations.
(
iv
)
The degree of common ownership or financial control over the entities.
(
v
)
Any other factor as determined by the department.
(i) "On-call shift" means any time that an employer
requires an employee to be available to work or to contact the employer or wait
to be contacted by the employer for determining if the employee must report to
work, regardless of whether the employee is located on the employer's premises.
(j) "Regular rate of pay" means the regular hourly
rate or hourly equivalent that an employer must pay an employee for each hour
the employee works during a given work shift, including any shift differential
pay. Regular rate of pay does not include any of the following:
(
i
)
Tips.
(
ii
)
Bonuses or other incentive payments.
(
iii
)
Overtime, holiday pay, or any other premium rate.
(
iv
)
Additional compensation required under section 11 or 15.
(k) "Retail establishment" means the fixed point of
sale location for a retail trade establishment as that term is used in codes
441110 to 453998 of the 2012 North American Industry Classification System.
(
l
)
"Shift differential pay" means a pay differential meant to compensate
an employee for work performed under differing conditions, such as for working
at night. Shift differential pay does not include any additional compensation
an employer is required to pay an employee under section 11 or 15.
(m) "Successor employer" means an employer that is
substantially the same entity as a predecessor employer as determined by
criteria established by the department.
(n) "Time of hire" means the period after an
acceptance of an offer of employment but before commencement of the employment.
(o) "Work schedule" means the hours, days, and
times, including regular work shifts and on-call shifts, when an employee is
required by an employer to perform duties of employment for which the employee
will receive compensation.
(p) "Work shift" means the specific and consecutive
hours the employer requires the employee to work.
(q) "Workweek" means a fixed period of time
established by an employer that reflects a regularly recurring period of 168
hours or 7 consecutive 24-hour periods. A workweek may begin on any day of the
week and any hour of the day and need not coincide with a calendar week, and
the beginning of a workweek may change if the change is intended to be
permanent.
(r) "Writing" means and "written"
describes a printed or printable communication in physical or electronic format
including a communication that is transmitted through
email,
text message, or a computer system or is otherwise sent and stored
electronically.
(s) "Year" means any fixed consecutive 12-month
period of time.
Sec. 5. (1) An employer
shall provide a new employee with a written good-faith estimate of the
employee's work schedule at the time of hire. An employer shall provide the
good-faith estimate in the language the employer typically uses to communicate
with the employee. The good-faith estimate must include all of the following
information
:
(a) The median number of hours the employee can expect to work
in a typical 1-month period.
(b)
A statement regarding
if and when
an employee can expect to work on-call
shifts
.
(c) The written notice required under section 9.
(2) A good-faith estimate described in subsection (1) may be
based on a prior year schedule if it is an estimate of seasonal or episodic
work.
Sec. 9. (1) Except as
otherwise provided in subsection (4), an employer shall provide an employee
with a written work schedule
not less than
14
calendar days before the first day of the work schedule. The employer shall
post the written work schedule in a conspicuous location that is accessible to
employees. An employer shall provide a written work schedule that runs through
the last date of the posted work schedule in effect at the time of delivery to
the following employees at the following times:
(a) For a new employee, on or before the employee's first day
of work.
(b) For an employee on a leave of absence, on the employee's
first day of work after the leave of absence.
(2) A written work schedule must meet all of the following
requirements:
(a) Be in English and in the language the employer typically
uses to communicate with its employees.
(b) Include all work shifts and on-call shifts for the work
period.
(3) After providing the advance notice required under
subsection (1), an employer shall not change a written work schedule unless the
employer has provided the employee with timely notice of the change in writing
or by in-person conversation or telephone call. An employee may decline any
work shifts not included in the employee's written work schedule.
(4) At any time after the advance notice of written work
schedule required under this section
is provided to
an employee
,
the
employee may request
in writing that the employer add the employee to 1 or more work shifts or
on-call work shifts. A change to the employee's written work schedule resulting
from an employee-requested work schedule change is not subject to the advance notice
required under this section.
Sec. 11. (1) Subject to
subsection (2), an employer shall not schedule or require an employee to work
during either of the following rest periods:
(a) The
12
hours immediately
following the end of the previous calendar day's work shift or on-call shift.
(b) The
12
hours immediately
following the end of a work shift or on-call shift that spanned 2 calendar
days.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the employee agrees in
writing to work during the rest period.
(3) An employer shall compensate an employee for each hour or
portion of an hour that the employee works during a rest period described in
subsection (1) at 1.5 times the employee's regular rate of pay. This subsection
does not apply to any hour or portion of an hour during which an employee
provides roadside assistance services. As used in this subsection,
"roadside assistance" means off-site repair assistance rendered to a
motorist with a disabled vehicle.
Sec. 13. At the time of
hire and during employment, an employee may identify any limitations or changes
in the employee's work schedule availability. The employee may also request not
to be scheduled for work shifts during certain times or at certain locations.
An employer may require the employee to provide reasonable verification of the
need for a request made under this section. The employer shall pay any
reasonable costs for providing medical verification, including lost wages, that
are not paid under a health benefit plan in which the employee is enrolled. An
employer is not required to grant an employee's request under this section. An
employer shall not retaliate against an employee for making a request under
this section.
Sec. 15. (1) An employer
shall provide the following compensation to an employee for each
employer-initiated change that occurs to the employee's written work schedule
without the advance notice required under section 9:
(a) 1 hour of pay at the employee's regular rate of pay, in
addition to any wages earned, in any of the following circumstances:
(
i
)
More than 30 minutes of work are added to the employee's work shift.
(
ii
)
The date or start or end time of the employee's shift is changed with no loss
of hours.
(
iii
)
The employee is scheduled for an additional shift or on-call shift.
(b) The greater of the minimum wage rate established under
section 4 of the improved workforce opportunity wage act, 2018 PA 338, MCL
408.934, or 0.5 times the employee's regular rate of pay per hour for each hour
that the employee does not work in any of the following circumstances:
(
i
)
Hours are subtracted from the employee's work shift before or after the
employee reports for work.
(
ii
)
The date or start or end time of the employee's shift is changed, resulting in
a loss of hours.
(
iii
)
The employee's work shift is canceled.
(
iv
)
The employer does not ask the employee to perform work while the employee is
scheduled for an on-call shift.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply to any of the following
circumstances:
(a) An employer subtracts hours from an employee's work
schedule for disciplinary reasons for just cause, if the employer documents the
incident leading to the employee's discipline in writing.
(b) An employee's work shift or on-call shift cannot begin or
continue because of any of the following:
(
i
)
A threat to employees or property.
(
ii
)
The recommendation of a public official.
(
iii
)
Failure of a public utility to supply electricity, water, or natural gas or
there is a failure in the public utilities or sewer system.
(
iv
)
A natural disaster or a similar cause not within the employer's control.
(
v
)
A ticketed event is canceled, rescheduled, or changes in duration because of
circumstances that are outside the employer's control.
(c)
An employer requests that
an employee work additional hours to address unanticipated customer needs or
unexpected employee absence and
both
of the
following conditions are met:
(
i
)
The employee consents in writing to work the additional hours.
(
ii
)
If
the employee is working a work shift at the time the employer makes the
request, the employer makes the request either individually or as part of a
group communication
,
or if the employee is not
working a work shift at the time the employer makes the request, the employer
makes the request through a group communication.
(3) As used in this section:
(a) "Group communication" means
written or oral
communication to all eligible
employees
.
(b) "Ticketed event" means a sporting,
entertainment, civic, charitable, or other event that requires a ticket for
admission. The ticket may be electronic
or
physical
or a name on a list held by the event organizer.
Sec. 17. The department
shall make available to employers a poster that includes the rights of
employees under this act. An employer shall display the poster at its workplace
so that it is reasonably conspicuous and accessible. If displaying the poster is
not feasible
,
including, but not limited to,
situations in which an employer's employees work remotely or do not have a
regular workplace or job site, the employer shall provide the poster on an
individual basis in a physical or electronic format.
Sec. 19. An employer
shall retain records that document the employer's compliance with this act for
not less than 5
years.
Sec. 21. An employer
shall not do any of the following:
(a) Interfere with, restrain, deny, or attempt to deny the
exercise of any right protected under this act.
(b) Retaliate or in any way discriminate against an individual
with respect to hire, tenure, or any other term or condition of employment
because the individual has inquired about the provisions of this act.
Sec. 23. (1) An
individual aggrieved by a violation of this act may do either of the following:
(a) File a complaint with the department.
(b) Bring a civil action for appropriate injunctive relief or
damages, or both, in the circuit court for the county where the alleged
violation occurred or where the person against whom the civil complaint is
filed resides or
the person's
principal place
of business
is located
. Filing a complaint
with the department under subdivision (a) is not a prerequisite or a bar to
bringing an action under this subdivision.
(2) The department shall investigate a complaint it receives
under subsection (1). Upon completion of its investigation, the department
shall issue a written determination to the complainant and alleged violator
that states whether a violation occurred and includes the information the
department relied on in making its determination.
Sec. 25. (1) This act
does not do any of the following:
(a) Limit an employee's rights or protections otherwise
provided by law.
(b) Prohibit an employer from providing an employee with
greater rights or benefits
,
including, but not
limited to, compensation and notice, than what is required under this act.
(c) Provide a cause of action to an employee for work schedule
changes necessary to accommodate that employee under either of the following:
(
i
)
The
earned sick time act,
2018 PA 338, MCL
408.961 to 408.974.
(
ii
)
The family and medical leave act, 29 USC chapter 28.
(2) This act applies to a collective bargaining agreement that
is entered into, extended, or renewed on or after the effective date of this
act.
Sec. 27. The department
may promulgate rules to implement this act
under
the
administrative procedures act of 1969, 1969 PA 306, MCL 24.201 to 24.328.
Sec. 29. (1) An employer that employs 250 or more employees
shall comply with this act beginning not later than 1 year after the effective
date of this act.
(2) An employer that employs 100 or
more employees but fewer than 250 employees shall comply with this act
beginning not later than 2 years after the effective date of this act.
(3) An employer that employs 50 or
more employees but fewer than 100 employees shall comply with this act
beginning not later than 3 years after the effective date of this act.
(4) An employer that employs 20 or
more employees but fewer than 50 employees shall comply with this act beginning
not later than 4 years after the effective date of this act.

2026-HB-5955.title: House Bill 5955 of 2026
2026-HB-5955.subject: Labor: fair employment practices; labor service agencies; regulate. Creates new act.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Kara Hope

2026-HB-5955.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 5955
A bill to regulate temporary labor service
agencies, the clients of temporary labor service agencies, and temporary
laborers; to prohibit retaliation for exercising rights granted under this act;
to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental officers
and entities; to provide for the promulgation of rules; and to provide remedies
and sanctions.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. This act may be
cited as the "temporary laborer rights act".
Sec. 3. As used in this
act:
(a) "Client" means a person that contracts with a
temporary labor service organization to obtain the services of temporary
laborers.
(b) "Department" means the department of licensing
and regulatory affairs.
(c) "Job site" means the physical location at which
a temporary laborer performs work for a client under a contract between a
temporary labor service agency and the client.
(d) "Temporary labor" means work performed by a
temporary laborer at a job site, the duration of which may be specific or
undefined, under a contract between a temporary labor service agency and a
client. Temporary labor does not include professional work.
(e) "Temporary labor service agency" means a person
engaged in the business of employing temporary laborers to provide services,
for a fee, to or for a client under a contract with the client.
(f) "Temporary laborer" means an individual who
contracts for
temporary labor
with a temporary
labor service agency.
Sec. 5. (1) A temporary
labor service agency shall provide a temporary laborer, at the time of dispatch
to a client, with a notice
that includes
all
of the following on a form approved by the department:
(a) The name of each temporary laborer dispatched to the same
job site.
(b) The name and nature of the work to be performed and the
types of equipment, protective clothing, and training that are required for the
work.
(c) The wage rate for the work.
(d) The name and address of the client and job site.
(e) The terms of the transportation to the job site.
(f) Whether a meal or equipment is provided by the temporary
labor service agency or the client and the cost of the meal and equipment.
(2) If a temporary laborer is assigned to the same assignment
for more than 1 day, the temporary labor service agency is required to provide
the notice under subsection (1) on the first day and any day the terms of the
notice change.
(3) If a temporary laborer is not placed with a client or
otherwise contracted to work for a day that the temporary laborer reports to
the temporary labor service agency, the temporary labor service agency shall,
on
the request of the temporary laborer, provide the
temporary laborer with confirmation that the temporary laborer sought work. The
confirmation must be signed by an employee of the temporary labor service
agency and include the name of the agency, the name and address of the
temporary laborer, and the date and time that the temporary laborer received
the confirmation.
(4) A temporary labor service agency shall not provide a
temporary laborer to a job site where a strike, lockout, or other labor dispute
exists.
(5) The department shall encourage a temporary labor service
agency to hire employees who can communicate the information required under
subsections (1) to (3) in the languages that are generally understood in the
geographic area of the temporary labor service agency.
Sec. 7. (1) A temporary
labor service agency shall maintain a record of each transaction with a client
that includes all of the following information:
(a) The name, address, and telephone number of the client, the
job sites to which temporary laborers were sent by the temporary labor service
agency, and the date of the transaction.
(b) All of the following information for each temporary
laborer:
(
i
)
The temporary laborer's name and address.
(
ii
)
The job sites to which the temporary laborer was assigned.
(
iii
)
The number of hours worked by the temporary laborer and the temporary laborer's
wage rate.
(
iv
)
The name and nature of the work performed by the temporary laborer.
(c) The name and title of the employee responsible for the
transaction.
(d) The number of hours billed to the client.
(e) The specific qualifications or attributes of a temporary
laborer requested by the client.
(f) Copies of all contracts with the client and copies of all
invoices for the client.
(g) Copies of all notices provided under section 5(1).
(h) All deductions from each temporary laborer's compensation
made by the client or temporary labor service agency
,
including, but not limited to, the temporary laborer's transportation, food,
equipment, withheld income tax, and withheld Social Security payments.
(i) Verification of the actual cost of any equipment or meal
charged to a temporary laborer.
(j) The race and gender of each temporary laborer, as provided
by the temporary laborer.
(k) Any other information as required by the department.
(2) A client shall remit the information described in
subsection (1) in its possession to a temporary labor service agency
not later than
7 days after the last day of the work
week worked by a temporary laborer. The failure of a client to remit this
information to a temporary labor service agency is not a defense to a violation
of this section.
(3) A temporary labor service agency shall maintain records
under subsection (1) for 7 years after
the date the
records are created.
A temporary labor service agency shall make the
records available for inspection by the department during normal business
hours. A temporary labor service agency shall make the records described in
subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (g), (h), and (i) available for review or copying
by the respective temporary laborer during normal business hours
not later than
5 days after the temporary laborer
requests the records. A temporary labor service agency shall make forms, in
duplicate, for requests made under this subsection available to temporary
laborers at the dispatch office, and shall provide a copy of the request form
to the temporary laborer.
(4) A person shall not make a false, inaccurate, or incomplete
entry into a record required under this section or delete required information
from a record.
A
client
that does not
remit records to the temporary labor
service agency under subsection (2)
violates
this
section
unless the client was precluded from
remitting the records for reasons beyond
the client's
control.
Sec. 9. A temporary labor
service agency or client shall not charge a temporary laborer for a meal that
the temporary labor service agency or client provides to the temporary laborer
and that the temporary laborer does not consume. If a temporary labor service
agency or client provides a meal to a temporary laborer and the temporary
laborer consumes, wholly or partially, the meal, the temporary labor service
agency or client may charge
the temporary laborer
only
the actual cost of the meal. The purchase of a meal must not be a condition of
employment for a temporary laborer.
Sec. 11. (1) A temporary
labor service agency or client shall not charge a fee to transport a temporary
laborer to or from a job site. A temporary labor service agency is responsible
for the conduct and performance of a person
that
transports
a temporary laborer to or from the temporary labor service agency to a job
site, unless the
person
is any of the
following:
(a) A public mass transportation system.
(b) A common carrier.
(c) The temporary laborer providing
the
temporary laborer's
own transportation.
(d) Selected exclusively by and at the sole choice of the
temporary laborer for transportation in a vehicle not owned or operated by the
temporary labor service agency.
(2) If a temporary labor service agency provides
transportation to a temporary laborer or refers a temporary laborer to a person
for transportation under subsection (3), the temporary labor service agency
shall not allow a motor vehicle to be used for the transportation if the
temporary labor service agency knows or should know that the motor vehicle is
unsafe or not equipped as required under this act. This subsection does not
apply to a motor vehicle that is any of the following:
(a) The property of a public mass transportation system.
(b) The property of a common carrier.
(c) The temporary laborer's personal vehicle.
(d) The vehicle of a temporary laborer used to transport other
temporary laborers and that is selected exclusively by and at the sole choice
of the temporary laborer for transportation.
(3) A temporary labor service agency shall not refer a
temporary laborer to a person for transportation to or from a job site unless
that person is a public mass transportation system or will provide the
transportation at no charge. Directing a temporary laborer to accept
transportation from a specific temporary laborer as a condition of work is a
referral by the temporary labor service agency under this subsection. Any
mention or discussion by a temporary labor service agency of the cost of
transportation provided by another temporary laborer is a referral under this
subsection. Informing a temporary laborer of the availability of transportation
provided by another temporary laborer is not a referral under this subsection.
(4) A temporary labor service agency that provides
transportation for a temporary laborer to a job site shall also provide the
temporary laborer transportation from the job site, unless the temporary
laborer agrees, before departure to the job site, to obtain an alternative
means of transportation from the job site.
Sec. 13. (1)
Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a
temporary
labor service agency or client shall not charge a temporary laborer
for
any safety equipment, clothing, accessory, or
other item temporarily provided to a temporary laborer that is required by law,
custom, or the client to perform the work
. If
the
temporary laborer
does not
return the item
, the temporary labor service agency or client may charge
the temporary laborer not more than the market value of the item
.
(2) If a temporary labor service agency makes available to a
temporary laborer for purchase an item other than those described in subsection
(1), the temporary labor service agency shall not charge more than the actual
market value for the item.
Sec. 15. (1) A temporary
labor service agency shall include on a temporary laborer's paycheck stub, or
with the temporary laborer's paycheck stub on a form approved by the
department, all of the following information:
(a) The name, address, and telephone number of each client for
which the temporary laborer worked. If this information is provided on the
temporary laborer's paycheck stub, a code for each client may be used if the
required information for each coded client is made available to the temporary
laborer.
(b) The number of hours worked by the temporary laborer at
each client each day during the pay period. If the temporary laborer is
assigned to work at the same job site of the same client for multiple days in
the same work week, the temporary labor service agency may record a summary of
hours worked at that client's job site if the first and last day of that work
week are also identified.
(c) The wage rate for each hour worked, including premium
rates and bonuses.
(d) The total pay period earnings.
(e) All deductions from the temporary laborer's compensation
made by the client or the temporary labor service agency, and the purpose for
which deductions were made, including, but not limited to, transportation,
food, equipment, withheld income tax, and withheld Social Security payments.
(f) Any additional information as required by the department.
(2) A client shall provide
to
a temporary laborer, at the end of a work day, a work verification form that
includes the date, the temporary laborer's name, the job site location, and the
hours worked on that day. The department shall prescribe a form for a client to
use under this subsection. A client that violates this subsection may be
ordered to pay a civil fine of not more than $500.00. For a second and any
subsequent violation, a client may be ordered to pay a civil fine of not more
than
$2,500.00. Each violation of this subsection
for each temporary laborer and for each day the violation continues is a
separate and distinct violation.
The prosecutor of
the county in which the violation occurred or the attorney general may bring an
action to collect the fine.
(3) Not later than February 1 of each year, a temporary labor
service agency shall provide a temporary laborer with an earnings summary for
the immediately preceding calendar year. A temporary labor service agency
shall, at the time of each wage payment, give notice to a temporary laborer of
the availability of the annual earnings summary or, as an alternative, post a
notice of the availability of the annual earnings summary in a conspicuous
place in its public access area.
(4) A temporary labor service agency or client shall not
charge a temporary laborer for the expense of conducting a consumer report, as
that term is defined in 15 USC 1681a(d), a criminal background check, or a drug
test.
(5) The total amount deducted from a temporary laborer's
compensation by a temporary labor service agency or a client for meals or
equipment must not cause a temporary laborer's hourly wage rate to fall below
the minimum wage rate established under the improved workforce opportunity wage
act, 2018 PA 337, MCL 408.931 to 408.945.
(6) If a temporary laborer who is contracted by a temporary
labor service agency to work at a client's job site
does
not
,
at the
direction of the client, perform work for
the client, the temporary
labor service agency shall pay the temporary laborer an amount equal to
not less than
4 hours of pay at the agreed
on
wage rate. However, if the temporary labor
service agency contracts the temporary laborer to work at another job site
during the same shift, the temporary labor service agency shall pay the temporary
laborer an amount equal to
not less than
2
hours of pay at the agreed
on
wage rate.
Sec. 17. A temporary
labor service agency shall attempt to place a temporary laborer into a
permanent position with a client if the client informs the temporary labor
service agency of its plan to hire a permanent employee for a position similar
to the positions for which temporary laborers are being provided by the agency
at the same job site.
Sec. 19. A temporary
labor service agency shall not restrict the right of a temporary laborer to
accept a permanent position with a client to whom the temporary laborer has
been referred for work or restrict the right of the client to offer employment
to the temporary laborer. If the temporary laborer accepts a permanent position
with the client, the temporary labor service agency may charge a placement fee
to the client. The fee must not exceed an amount equal to the total daily
commission rate the temporary labor service agency would have received over a
60-day period, reduced by an amount equal to the daily commission rate the
temporary labor service agency is entitled to receive for each day the
temporary laborer performed work for the temporary labor service agency in the
immediately preceding 12 months.
Sec. 21. A temporary
labor service agency shall provide adequate seating in the public access area
of the offices of the temporary labor service agency. All notice posting
required under this act must be posted in the public access area. The public
access area must allow for access to restrooms and water.
Sec. 23. (1) A temporary
labor service agency shall register with the department
in accordance with
this section and
the
procedures established by the department. A temporary labor service
agency shall provide proof of an unemployment
insurance
agency account number issued under the Michigan employment security act,
1936 (Ex Sess) PA 1, MCL 421.1 to 421.75, and proof of insurance that complies
with section 611 of the worker's disability compensation act of 1969, 1969 PA
317, MCL 418.611. If a temporary labor service agency's insurance coverage
lapses, the temporary labor service agency shall report the lapse of coverage
to the department, and the department shall suspend the temporary labor service
agency's registration until the lapse ends.
(2) The department may assess a temporary labor service agency
a nonrefundable registration fee of not more than $1,000.00 per year and a
nonrefundable fee of not more than $250.00 for each branch office or location
where the temporary labor service agency regularly contracts with temporary
laborers for services. The department may charge an additional fee if the
temporary labor service agency issues or delivers a check to the department
that is not honored by the financial institution
on
which
it is drawn.
(3) At the time of registration and every year after that, a
temporary labor service agency shall submit to the department a report that
includes the information listed in section 7(1), categorized by branch office,
in the aggregate for all temporary laborers, on a form as prescribed by the
department. The department shall aggregate the information submitted by all
temporary labor service agencies and make the information available to the
public only on a municipal and county basis. The department shall remove all
identifying data before making the information available. The information and
reports submitted to the department under this subsection are exempt from
disclosure under the freedom of information act, 1976 PA 442, MCL 15.231 to
15.246. As used in this subsection, "identifying data" means
information that does
1 or both
of the
following:
(a) Provides information regarding a temporary laborer or
temporary laborer's service agency's identity.
(b) Identifies clients
contracting
with
a temporary labor service agency or other information that can be
traced to a specific temporary labor service agency or its client.
(4) The department shall create and maintain all of the
following at regular intervals on its public website:
(a) A list of all registered temporary labor service agencies
whose registration is in good standing.
(b) A list of temporary labor service agencies whose
registration has been suspended, including the reason for the suspension, the
date the suspension was initiated, and
,
if
known,
the date
the suspension will be lifted.
(c) A list of temporary labor service agencies whose
registration has been revoked, including the reason for the revocation and the
date the registration was revoked.
(5) A temporary labor service agency shall post at each of its
branch offices, in a position easily accessible to all temporary laborers,
notices as supplied and required by the department that include a copy or
summary of the provisions of this act and a toll-free telephone number for
persons to contact the department regarding this act.
(6) A temporary labor service agency that violates subsection
(1) may be ordered to pay a civil fine of not more than $500.00. For a
continuing violation, each day the violation continues is a separate and
distinct violation.
The prosecutor of the county in
which the violation occurred or the attorney general may bring an action to
collect the fine.
Sec. 25. A person is not
eligible to register a temporary labor service agency under this act if the
person or any of its officers, directors, partners, or managers or any owner of
25% or more of a beneficial interest has been involved, as an owner, officer,
director, partner, or manager of a temporary labor service agency whose
registration has been revoked or suspended, without being reinstated, within
the 5 years immediately preceding the filing of the registration.
Sec. 27. (1) The
department shall enforce this act. The department shall conduct investigations
in connection with the administration and enforcement of this act. To ensure
compliance with this act, an investigator of the department may inspect, at any
reasonable time, a location covered by this act or a contract for the
employment of a temporary laborer entered into by a client.
(2) The department shall conduct all hearings under this act
in accordance with
the contested case procedures of
the administrative procedures act of 1969, 1969 PA 306, MCL 24.201 to 24.328,
to determine whether a person violated this act. If the department determines
that a person violated this act, the department may do any of the following:
(a) Issue and cause to be served on a person an order to cease
and desist from further violating this act.
(b) Take appropriate action to eliminate the effect of the
violation.
(c) Deny, suspend, or revoke a registration under this act.
Sec
29.
An individual
aggrieved by a violation of this act may do either of the following:
(a) File a complaint with the department.
(b) Bring a civil action for appropriate injunctive relief or
damages, or both, in the circuit court for the county where the alleged
violation occurred or where the person against whom the civil complaint is
filed resides or
where the person's
principal
place of business
is located
. Filing a
complaint with the department under subdivision (a) is not a prerequisite or a
bar to bringing an action under this subdivision.
Sec.
31.
(1) A client shall not enter into a contract
with a temporary labor service agency unless the temporary labor service agency
is registered under this act. A client shall verify a temporary labor service
agency's registration with the department before entering into a contract with
the temporary labor service agency, and on March 1 and September 1 of each
year. A temporary labor service agency shall provide each of its clients with
proof of valid registration at the time of entering into a contract. A
temporary labor service agency shall notify, by telephone and in writing, each
temporary laborer it employs and each client with whom it has a contract
not later than
24 hours after a denial, suspension,
or revocation of its registration. If a temporary labor service agency's
registration is denied, suspended, or revoked, the temporary labor service
agency may
not
enforce a contract with a
client beginning
on
the date
the
denial, suspension, or revocation becomes
effective and until the temporary labor service agency becomes registered and
is
considered in good standing by the department.
(2)
On
the request of a
client, the department shall provide to the client a list of registered
temporary labor service agencies. The department shall provide on its public
website a list of registered temporary labor service agencies. A client may
rely on information provided by the department or maintained on the
department's public website and must be held harmless if the information
maintained or provided by the department was inaccurate.
(3) A client that violates this section may be ordered to pay
a civil fine of not more than $500.00. Each day during which a client contracts
with a temporary labor service agency not registered under this act is a
separate and distinct violation.
The prosecutor of
the county in which the violation occurred or the attorney general may bring an
action to collect the fine.
Sec.
33.
A person shall not retaliate or discriminate
against an individual because the individual does or is about to do any of the
following:
(a) File a complaint under this act.
(b) Testify, assist, or participate in an investigation,
proceeding, or action concerning a violation of this act.
(c) Oppose a violation of this act.
Sec.
35.
The department may promulgate rules to implement
this act
under
the administrative procedures
act of 1969, 1969 PA 306, MCL 24.201 to 24.328.

2026-HB-6056.title: House Bill 6056 of 2026
2026-HB-6056.subject: Labor: collective bargaining; poster of collective bargaining rights; require certain employers to display at work sites and provide to employees. Amends1939 PA 176(MCL423.1-423.30) by adding sec. 8.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Dylan Wegela

2026-HB-6056.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 6056
A bill to amend 1939 PA 176, entitled
"An act to create a commission relative to labor
disputes, and to prescribe its powers and duties; to provide for the mediation
and arbitration of labor disputes, and the holding of elections thereon; to
regulate the conduct of parties to labor disputes and to require the parties to
follow certain procedures; to regulate and limit the right to strike and
picket; to protect the rights and privileges of employees, including the right
to organize and engage in lawful concerted activities; to protect the rights
and privileges of employers; to make certain acts unlawful; to make
appropriations; and to prescribe means of enforcement and penalties for
violations of this act,"
(MCL 423.1 to 423.30) by adding section 8a.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 8a. (1) An
employer shall do both of the following:
(a) Display the poster described in subsection (2) at each of the
employer's work sites in a prominent location that is accessible to each of the
employer's employees.
(b) Make the poster described in subsection (2) available to each of the
employer's employees in a digital format via an internal website or email.
(2) The department of labor and economic opportunity shall create and
make available to employers a poster that describes all of the rights granted
to an employee under the national labor relations act of 1935, 29 USC 151 to
169. The poster must be in English and any other language requested by a labor
organization or employer. The department of labor and economic opportunity
shall use publications from the National Labor Relations Board in creating the
poster and may request assistance from the National Labor Relations Board in
creating the poster.
(3) An employer that violates subsection (1) is subject to a civil fine
as follows:
(a) For a first violation, $5,000.00.
(b) For a second or subsequent violation, $10,000.00.
(4) The
prosecutor of the county in which the violation occurred or the attorney
general may bring an action to collect a civil fine under this section. A civil
fine collected under this section must be deposited in the general fund.

2026-HB-6057.title: House Bill 6057 of 2026
2026-HB-6057.subject: Labor: working conditions; suitable seats; require employers to provide to employees under certain circumstances. Creates new act.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Dylan Wegela

2026-HB-6057.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 6057
A bill to require employers to provide suitable seats for
employees under certain circumstances; to provide for the powers and duties of
certain local and state governmental officers and entities; to provide for the
promulgation of rules; and to provide civil sanctions.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. As used in this
act:
(a) "Department" means the department of labor and
economic opportunity.
(b) "Employee" means an individual employed by an
employer.
(c) "Employer" means a person that employs 1 or more
employees.
(d) "Person" means an individual or a partnership,
corporation, limited liability company, association, governmental entity, or
other legal entity.
(e) "Suitable seat" means
any of the following that has support for an individual's back:
(
i
) A
chair.
(
ii
) A
stool.
(
iii
)
A bench.
(
iv
)
Any other similar object on which an individual can sit.
Sec. 3. (1)
Subject to subsection (2), an
employer shall provide
to
an employee
who
is performing work for the employer at a location that is owned, leased, or
operated by or under the control of the employer
a suitable seat if it
is reasonable for the employee to use a
suitable
seat
while performing
the
work
.
This section applies regardless
of whether the employee is required to stand to perform portions of the work.
(2) If it is not reasonable for an employee to use a
suitable
seat while performing
the
work
,
the
employer shall provide a suitable seat in close proximity to the employee's
working area. An employer shall not prohibit an employee from using a
suitable
seat described in this subsection unless
the employee is actively performing
the
work.
Sec. 5. An employer that
violates this act is
subject to a civil fine of
$250.00 multiplied by the number of employees aggrieved by the violation per
2-week period that the employer remains in violation. The prosecutor of the
county in which the violation occurred or the attorney general may bring an
action to collect the fine. A fine collected under this section must be
deposited in the general fund.
Sec. 7. The department may
promulgate rules to implement this act under the administrative procedures act
of 1969, 1969 PA 306, MCL 24.201 to 24.328.
Sec. 9. If a collective
bargaining agreement or other employment agreement meets both of the following
conditions, this act applies to the parties to the agreement beginning on the
date the agreement expires or is terminated, amended, extended, or renewed:
(a) The agreement is in effect on the effective date of this
act.
(b) The agreement conflicts with this act.

2026-HB-6070.title: House Bill 6070 of 2026
2026-HB-6070.subject: Labor: other; registry of employers who relocate a call center to a foreign country; require the department of labor and economic opportunity to create. Creates new act.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. James DeSana

2026-HB-6070.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 6070
A bill to create the anti-offshoring accountability act; to
provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local governmental
officers and entities; to impose certain duties on certain employers; and to
prescribe civil sanctions.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. This act may be
cited as the
"anti-offshoring accountability
act".
Sec. 3. As used in this
act:
(a) "Call center" means a centralized office used
primarily for receiving or transmitting customer requests or inquiries by
telephone.
(b) "Department" means the department of
labor and economic opportunity.
(c) "Employer" means
a
person that meets both of the following conditions:
(
i
)
Employs,
either full-time or part-time, 50 or more individuals at a call
center.
(
ii

2026-HB-6088.title: House Bill 6088 of 2026
2026-HB-6088.subject: Labor: collective bargaining; tenants right to organize; provide for. Creates new act.

actions.description: introduced by Representative Rep. Emily Dievendorf

2026-HB-6088.full_text:
HOUSE BILL NO. 6088
A bill to establish the rights of tenants to organize tenant
unions; to prohibit certain conduct; to provide remedies and prescribe
penalties; and to provide for the powers and duties of certain state and local
governmental officers and entities.
the people of the state of michigan enact:
Sec. 1. This act may be
cited as the
"tenants right to organize
act".
Sec. 3. As used in this
act:
(a) "Common area" means a
portion of a rental premises that is generally accessible to all tenants.
Common area includes, but is not limited to, a hallway, a stairway, a laundry
and recreational room, a playground, a community center, a garage, or a
boundary fence.
(b)
"Landlord"
means that term as defined in section 1 of 1972 PA 348, MCL 554.601.
(c) "Rental agreement"
means an agreement that establishes or modifies the terms, conditions, rules,
regulations, or any other provisions concerning the use and occupancy of a
rental unit.
(d)
"Rental unit"
means a structure or part of a structure used as a home, residence, or sleeping
unit by a single
individual
or household unit,
or any grounds, or other facilities or
areas
promised
for the use of a residential tenant.
(e)
"Tenant" means
an individual who occupies a rental unit for residential purposes with the
landlord's consent for an agreed-upon consideration.
(f) "Tenant organizer"
means a person that assists tenants in organizing, forming, or operating a
tenant union and is not an employee or representative of the current or
prospective landlord.
(g) "Tenant union" means a
union organized or formed by tenants in residential premises that gives the
tenants the right to do all of the following:
(
i
)
Self-organize.
(
ii
) Join,
meet, and assist one another.
(
iii
)
Confer through representatives of the tenants' own choosing with a landlord.
(
iv
) Engage
in other concerted activities for the purpose of mutual aid and protection or refrain
from any concerted activity if the tenants choose.
(
v
)
Promulgate rules that govern the activities of the tenant union.
Sec. 5. Beginning on the
effective date of this act, tenants
have the right to
organize or form a tenant union. A tenant union may do all of the following:
(a) Distribute literature in common
areas in the rental premises.
(b) Place literature at or under
tenants' doors.
(c) Post information on bulletin
boards within the rental premises.
(d) Assist tenants to participate in
tenant organizational activities.
(e) Convene tenants meetings at any
reasonable time and in any appropriate space that would reasonably be
interpreted as areas that the tenants have access to under the tenants' rental
agreements, including a common area, the tenant's unit, if the tenant consents,
or other available space. A tenant union may permit electronic attendance of a
meeting convened under this act if a majority of the tenants in the tenant
union consent to the electronic attendance. A landlord shall not attend or make
audiorecordings of a meeting convened under this subdivision unless permitted
to do so by a majority of tenants in attendance.
(f) Formulate responses to the
landlord's actions, including rent or rent ceiling increases or requests for
rent or rent ceiling increases, proposed increases or decreases, or other
changes in the rental premises.
(g) Propose that the landlord modify
the rental premises' facilities and services.
(h) Engage in any other activity
reasonably related to the establishment or operation of a tenant union.
(i) Collect tenant union dues.
Sec.
7. (1) Tenants may engage the services of a tenant organizer to form a tenant
union.
(2) A tenant organizer may canvass
on behalf of the tenants in a multifamily rental premises. All of the following
apply to a tenant organizer's right to canvass in a multifamily rental
premises:
(a) If the multifamily rental
premises has a written policy that allows canvassing, a tenant organizer that
is not a tenant has the same privileges and rights of access as other uninvited
outside parties in the normal course of operations.
(b) If the multifamily rental
premises does not have a consistently enforced, written policy against
canvassing, the multifamily rental premises must be treated as if it has a
policy that allows canvassing.
(c) If a multifamily rental premises
has a consistently enforced, written policy against canvassing, a tenant shall
accompany the tenant organizer that is not a tenant while the tenant organizer
is canvassing within the multifamily rental premises. The tenant organizer that
is not a tenant has the same privileges and rights of access as other invited
outside parties in the normal course of operations.
Sec.
9. (1)
A landlord shall not
do
any of the following:
(a) Interfere
with the rights
of tenants
or a tenant organizer
under this
act.
(b) Threaten, penalize, or discriminate
or retaliate against a tenant that exercises the tenant's rights under this
act. Discriminatory or retaliatory conduct includes, but is not limited to,
intentionally delaying maintenance services, revoking access to community
amenities, or taking frivolous adverse actions against a tenant.
(c) Interfere with or delay the
investigation of a violation or the enforcement of this act.
(2) A landlord that violates
subsection (1) is subject to all of the following:
(a) A civil fine of not more than $1,000.00
for each violation.
(b) An injunctive order.
(c) Reasonable attorney fees.
(3) The attorney general, a tenant,
or a tenant organizer may bring an action to enforce this act in a court of
competent jurisdiction in the county where the defendant resides or does
business.
Sec.
11. If any portion of this act or the application of this act to any person or
circumstances is found invalid by a court, the invalidity must not affect the
remaining portions or applications of this act that can be given effect without
the invalid portion or application, if the remaining portions are not
determined by the court to be inoperative, and to this end this act is declared
to be severable.

2026-SB-0948.title: Senate Bill 948 of 2026
